items.final_answer: A smaller argument, moving toward the base case
items.prompt: In a recursive factorial function, what should each recursive call be given as its argument, relative to the current one, and why?
items.reference_answer: Each call must work on a smaller subproblem, so the argument gets smaller (e.g. n-1 for factorial). This moves the calls toward the base case so the recursion can stop. Final answer: A smaller argument, moving toward the base case.
rubric: Links this to reaching the base case
wrong_texts: Passes the same or a larger argument, so the calls never approach the base case.

items.final_answer: The call stack overflows
items.prompt: A function calls itself but each call receives the same input as before. Predict what happens when it runs and explain.
items.reference_answer: The call is not on a smaller subproblem, so it never reaches a base case. The calls keep stacking on the call stack until it overflows. Final answer: The call stack overflows.
rubric: Notes the input never gets smaller so no base case is reached
wrong_texts: Thinks the function will eventually stop or return on its own.
